text:
Marisol: Quick sync — I'm drafting the PRD for the Dedicated Capacity launch. Need to resolve SLA targets per commitment tier, autoscale fallback behavior, and acceptance criteria for canary. Also folding in customer asks from Acme and Nova: guaranteed burst headroom, billing granularity, and isolation guarantees. Thoughts?

Kevin: For baseline sizing my take — map tiers to reserved GPUs and per-route min concurrency. Suggest we define p50/p95 latency targets by model class rather than a single number.

Lina: Agree on model-class buckets. Operationally we need a clear failure-mode in the PRD: when warm pool is exhausted, automatic fallback to a compatible lower-SKU variant + throttling thresholds. Cold-starts for KV cache are the biggest risk.

Anya: Customers pushed for billing alignment — e.g., commitment tier discount if we hit p95 < 300ms under 80% committed load. Do we want that explicit in acceptance criteria or keep it a sales appendix?

Marisol: I think explicit makes acceptance testing easier. Draft acceptance criteria suggestion: 
- p95 latency <= 300ms for "standard" text-gen (<=1k tokens) under committed throughput
- Throughput guarantees expressed as RPS per committed GPU per model class (numbers TBD)
- Graceful degradation: when capacity constrained, fallback path must keep error-rate uplift < 2% measured by synthetic checks
- Canary gate: must show no P99 errors for a rolling 15m window during canary or auto-rollback triggers

Kevin: Adding an autoscale policy example to the PRD might help align eng + infra. Something like: 
```
policy:
  min_instances: committed_gpus
  max_instances: committed_gpus + burst_pool
  scale_up: target_cpu>70% || queue_len>10
  scale_down: idle>300s
  warm_pool: 10% of max_instances
```
(we'll tune thresholds after perf tests)

Lina: Edge cases to call out explicitly in the PRD:
- Sustained 3x burst lasting >10 minutes -> trigger ops paging and throttle non-committed tenants
- KV cache hotflip: very large contexts can blow mem -> enforce context-length cap or route to high-memory pool
- Model fallback correctness: ensure API returns clear signal when downgraded (header + metric) so clients can adapt

Marisol: Draft launch checklist (short):
- SLA doc signed by Sales + legal
- End-to-end canaries in prod playground for 48h with synthetic load tied to acceptance prompts
- Rollout plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% of committed routes, with automated rollback on canary failure
- Observability: per-route p95, queue length, warm-pool fill, fallback-rate, and billing deltas available in Console

deploy-bot: PRD created: https://redwood.internal/prd/DEDICATED-2028 (auto-generated)

Kevin: I'll add concrete throughput numbers and an initial cost amortization table by EOD.

Lina: I'll run a warm-pool sizing calc + a small sim and post results tomorrow morning. My initial rule-of-thumb: warm_pool >= 1 instance per 8 committed GPUs for typical gen workloads, but I'll validate.

Marisol: Great. @Kevin @Lina please flag blockers; otherwise I'll send draft to eng-review tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

Anya: Also loop in customer-billing and legal for exact commitment language before we finalize PRD.

Kevin: noted, will ping billing.

Marisol: Thanks — I'll update the PRD with these items and call out the open numbers as TODOs.
